milestone: M40 External Mode Pack Signer Trust Policy

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds runtime-owned trusted signer state and requires candidate approval to consume it.
Keeps signer trust policy in Rust and rejects valid-but-untrusted provenance signers before approval state is written.
Persists bounded trusted signer and approval evidence without raw candidate JSON, statements, signatures, or public keys.
Gives scheduled callers deterministic signer-trust next actions and fail-closed approval semantics.

answers.strategic_capabilities: mode_pack_runtime with support from runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: modepack.trustSigner records bounded trusted signer policy, and modepack.approveCandidate requires that trusted signer policy before writing approved remote Mode Pack candidate trust state.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M39 verifies provenance and requires it during approval, but any valid signer can still be approved because signer trust policy is not represented.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External candidates remain signed-but-not-authorized; Brownie cannot distinguish trusted signers from arbitrary valid signers.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M39.2 provenance-gated approval, M39.1 provenance verification, and M38.3 activation because it adds signer trust policy and consumes it at approval.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. Signer trust is a new state-changing policy mutation and cannot be represented by fetch, verify, approve, activate, or a summary wrapper.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds bounded mutation evidence only and no report, digest, history, readiness, preview, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime records trusted signer state and rejects approval unless the verified provenance signer is trusted.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers get deterministic trust-signer and approval routes and cannot accidentally approve arbitrary valid signers.
answers.milestone_progress: Establishes the core M40 signer trust boundary and may complete the minimal milestone if revocation is deferred.

exit_criteria: modepack.trustSigner records one bounded trusted signer policy entry with explicit authorization
signer trust replay returns the existing trust entry without duplicate ModePackSignerTrusted events
modepack.approveCandidate re-reads current trusted signer state for the verified provenance signer before writing approved state
approval rejects missing, stale, or mismatched trusted signer policy without writing approved candidate state
successful approval writes bounded approved candidate state carrying trusted signer handles
RPC and ledger payloads contain bounded metadata only and no raw candidate JSON, raw statement, raw signature bytes, or raw public key bytes
Behavior tests cover signer trust mutation, trust replay, untrusted approval denial, trusted approval success, bounded output, and VSIX validation

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M40.1 changes signer trust and approval behavior; review must confirm this is signer trust-gated approval, not a wrapper surface.
